newsitem.title: JAPAN: FUJI TV SEEN SET TO SPARKLE IN TOKYO BOURSE DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: FUJI TV SEEN SET TO SPARKLE IN TOKYO BOURSE DEBUT.

text.p: A track record of popular programmes and bright hopes for satellite broadcasting should ensure a sparkling debut for shares in Fuji Television Network Inc on the Tokyo bourse on Friday, analysts say.
The shares could soar to 700,000 yen against an initial offer price of 550,000 yen set late last month, brokers said.

"Fuji TV produces attractive programmes and has enough funds to survive the changing environment in Japan's broadcasting industry," said Nanako Sekiguchi, an industry analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
That includes Fuji TV's digital satellite plans. It announced earlier this year it would join media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's digital satellite broadcasting venture Japan Sky Broadcasting Co (JSkyB).

But some analysts said the euphoria over the stocks could fizzle out later for the same reason, as the market waits to see how much the satellite TV services contribute to the nationwide broadcaster's profits.
They said it could be a long time before the share price starts to factor in profits from the digital satellite business.

"It is true that Fuji TV has taken a clear step in entering the multi-channel era by joining JSkyB, but the day when the business contributes to Fuji's earnings is far away," said Yutaka Sugiyama, a senior analyst at UBS Securities Ltd.

Asked about Fuji TV's participation in JSkyB, Fuji TV president Hisashi Hieda said: "We hope the new business has a good impact on our results, but details of the new satellite broadcasting business have not yet been decided."
Brokers said that while Fuji TV's shares may jump to 700,000 yen, they are likely to settle a little lower.
"They should gradually stabilise slightly below 600,000 yen, with 630,000-640,000 yen the ceiling," Sugiyama said.
Fuji TV's initial share offer price was set at 550,000 yen on July 29, while the weighted average price of successful bids in the share auction held on the same day was 615,735 yen.
Besides the shares offered through the auction, Fuji TV will sell 84,000 new shares to add to an already issued 30,500 shares on the market.
Fuji TV said in May that its parent current profit for the year to March 1997 was 26.64 billion yen against 16.91 billion yen the previous year.

It expects lower profit of 22.70 billion yen for the current business year because of depreciation costs stemming from the transfer of its headquarters, but the steady profit increase should resume in the business year from next April, Fuji TV president Hieda said.
Of the six nationwide terrestrial broadcasting networks, only Tokyo Broadcasting System Inc and Nippon Television Network Corp are listed.
Some analysts also said trade in Fuji TV shares could be lower than it might otherwise be due to Nomura Securities Co Ltd's suspension of stock-related business.
The suspension is part of penalties imposed by the Finance Ministry for Nomura's illegal payoffs to a corporate racketeer.
